title: A Family of Parabolas and the Curve Traced by Their Vertices
originalTopic: Parameter families and the locus of vertices
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Plot the parabolas y = x^2 + cx + 1 for c = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 on one screen. Identify the common point through which every member passes, and find the equation of the curve on which all the vertices lie.

steps.title: Find the invariant point
steps.explanation: Changing c adds nothing at x = 0, so all five parabolas pass through (0, 1), which appears on screen as the point where the family crosses.
steps.why: Setting the parameter's coefficient to zero is the standard way to locate a base point of a family.

steps.title: Compute each vertex
steps.explanation: Completing the square gives y = (x + c/2)^2 + 1 - c^2/4, so the vertex coordinates in terms of c are (-c/2, 1 - c^2/4): for c = 0, 1, 2 the vertices are (0, 1), (-0.5, 0.75), (-1, 0).
steps.why: Vertex form exposes both the axis of symmetry and the minimum value as functions of the same parameter.

steps.title: Eliminate the parameter
steps.explanation: Substituting c = -2 x_v into y_v = 1 - c^2/4 removes c, leaving the downward parabola y = 1 - x^2 as the locus of the vertices.
steps.why: A locus is found by deleting the parameter, which converts the vertex formulas into a single relation between the coordinates.

steps.title: Verify graphically
steps.explanation: Drawing the five upward parabolas plus y = 1 - x^2 shows the lower curve passing exactly through each vertex and through the shared point (0, 1).
steps.why: The overlay turns an algebraic derivation into a visual check: if a vertex misses the curve, the elimination was wrong.
